description: §6.8.4 — E-TARE-BEFORE-DECL over-fire guard. The rule is BARE-FORM ONLY: `tare(@x, 0)` sets the reset default DIRECTLY and never consults the cell's init expression, so it works from any position — including above the cell's first write, which is exactly the position that is an error for the bare form. The sibling positive case (tare-before-decl-pos) is byte-identical apart from the second argument.
rationale: The rule's whole justification is 'at this point the cell has no init expression yet, so the call would do nothing'. That is a statement about the BARE form. The two-argument form lowers to `_scrml_default_set(key, () => expr)` — self-contained, never reading `_scrml_init_fns` — and §6.8.2 resolves default BEFORE init, so reset yields the named expression regardless of source position. Firing here rejected a valid program (S337 fix-round-2 finding 1, a regression the ordering check introduced); it landed green because neither the browser test nor the positive conformance case exercised the two-argument branch. A rule that discriminates between two forms needs a case per branch, which is what this pair is.
